2) Bullous pemphigoid — Important alternative. Classic in this age group and pruritic with widespread bullae, but DIF was negative and biopsy lacked the typical subepidermal blister with eosinophils, making it less likely but still possible (false-negative DIF can occur).  
3) Erythema multiforme / drug-related interface dermatitis (including early SJS spectrum) — Dyskeratotic necrotic keratinocytes and RBC extravasation can reflect interface/necrotic process from a drug; absence of clear mucosal involvement and lack of full-thickness epidermal necrosis argue against frank SJS/TEN.  
4) Generalized dyshidrotic/acute spongiotic eczema with secondary bullae (id reaction) — Fits initial palmar/plantar vesicles, prominent spongiosis on biopsy, pruritic course with subsequent generalization.  
5) Bullous fixed drug eruption — Can be antibiotic-triggered and produce localized bullae with epidermal necrosis; less consistent with the diffuse initial palmar/plantar presentation but remains possible.
